title: Tensor network Monte Carlo study of the J1-J2 Ising model on the square lattice
authors: Wanying Zheng, Tao Chen, Youjin Deng, Wanzhou Zhang
abstract: The frustrated square-lattice J1-J2 Ising model exhibits rich magnetic phases, yet its phase transitions remain difficult to characterize due to critical slowing down in conventional Monte Carlo and truncation errors inherent to tensor renormalization group methods.We develop a tensor-network Monte Carlo (TNMC) algorithm for this frustrated model, which supports both open and periodic boundary conditions. For periodic lattices, we use a sweeping block-update strategy that updates spin blocks while fixing surrounding spins.To boost efficiency, we couple our sampler with histogram reweighting, and test each technique standalone to validate these independent optimizations.We perform extensive finite-size scaling analyses at g=0.55 and g=1.0, extracting apparent critical temperatures and effective thermal exponents from Binder-cumulant data.Our method offers an efficient, nearly bias-free path for large-scale simulations of J1-J2-type frustrated magnets under periodic boundaries and generalizes readily to other frustrated spin lattices.
summary: This paper introduces a Tensor-network Monte Carlo (TNMC) algorithm to overcome the limitations of simulating the frustrated J1-J2 Ising model. By developing an efficient sampling technique, the authors perform finite-size scaling analyses to accurately determine critical temperatures and exponents. This provides a robust computational tool for studying frustrated magnetism in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: Characterizing the rich magnetic phases and phase transitions of the frustrated square-lattice J1-J2 Ising model, which is difficult due to critical slowing down in conventional Monte Carlo methods.
main_result: The developed Tensor-network Monte Carlo method successfully extracts apparent critical temperatures and effective thermal exponents for specific frustration ratios, showing consistency with theoretical predictions for continuous transitions.
method: The authors developed and applied a Tensor-network Monte Carlo (TNMC) algorithm, enhanced with histogram reweighting, to simulate the model efficiently.
model_or_system: The system is the frustrated square-lattice J1-J2 Ising model, described by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) couplings, characterized by the frustration ratio $g = J_2/|J_1|$.
key_observables: Binder cumulant $Q(T)$, apparent critical temperatures ($T_c$), and effective thermal exponents ($y_t$).
important_parameters: Frustration strengths $g = 0.55$ and $g = 1.0$; simulations cover both open and periodic boundary conditions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on finite-size scaling theory, and the authors note that the accessible system sizes limit definitive conclusions on the transition order at certain points.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the lattice structure, the tensor network contraction workflow (caching), and the results show Binder cumulant data used for finite-size scaling analysis.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical problem and the limitations of existing simulation techniques. It then details the construction and implementation of the TNMC algorithm, including tensor definitions and caching strategies. Finally, it applies the method to perform finite-size scaling analyses to extract critical parameters.
why_interesting: The development of TNMC provides a powerful, nearly bias-free numerical tool for simulating complex, frustrated magnetic systems, which is highly relevant for studying phase transitions in condensed matter models.
